#9514. 63 Christmas card messages, wishes, and greetings for all

Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA

Christmas is almost here, and it’s time to put together your family's holiday card. You’ve already done the work of choosing the perfect photo and selecting the design you like best, but now comes the hard part: writing the perfect message.

Even though you know how much a thoughtful greeting can brighten someone’s day, it’s not always easy to find the right words. It can be tough to strike the right balance between meaningful, caring, and sincere — but not too cheesy. (Okay, maybe a little cheesy!) Coming up with the right words to express your feelings can feel a little overwhelming. After all, every person in your life—your family, friends, coworkers, or even that special someone—deserves a message that feels meaningful and personal.

We know what you’re facing, so we’ve gathered together our favorite Christmas greetings to inspire you to write the perfect note for everyone on your list.

For many people, family is at the heart of the holiday season. It’s a great time to reflect on the love and memories you’ve shared and let your relatives know just how much they mean to you. Here are some ideas to help you express your gratitude as you wish your family members a very merry Christmas.

Have your parents been there through it all? Take a moment to show your appreciation in a way that feels natural and true to your relationship. Maybe your message will be lighthearted and jokey, or deep and moving — whatever suits the situation best.

“Merry Christmas, Mom and Dad! Thanks for always making the holidays feel magical — and for putting up with my crazy Christmas wish lists over the years. (There’s still time to get me those rollerskates, by the way!) You’re the best, and I hope you know how much I appreciate you.”

“Hope you’re ready for another Christmas where I eat most of the snacks and do none of the cooking. Love you both — thanks for everything you do to make the holidays special.”

Whether your relationship with your siblings is built on laughs, bickering, or a little of both, a Christmas message is the perfect way to show your love in a way that’s true to your bond.

“Merry Christmas to my partner-in-crime (and occasional sparring partner). Thanks for keeping life interesting and for always having my back. Love you!”

“Christmas wouldn’t be the same without you. Thanks for being the person who knows all my embarrassing moments and still chooses to hang out with me — although I guess you have to, because I know all your secrets, too! Hope your holidays are as awesome as you are.”

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas full of love, laughter, and minimal family drama. Here’s to another year of surviving the holidays together!”

For grandparents, aunts, uncles, or cousins, a thoughtful message can remind them how much you value them.

“Merry Christmas to my wonderful [grandma/grandpa/aunt/uncle/cousins]. You’ve always made the holidays so special, and I’m so lucky to have you in my life. Hope your Christmas is full of everything you love!”

“Wishing you all the joy and laughter the season can bring. You’re the heart of our family, and I’m so grateful for you this Christmas and every day.”

“Merry Christmas to the family who always knows how to keep things fun—and occasionally chaotic. (This year, I'm going to win our Christmas game of Monopoly — so don’t help [another relative] cheat!). Love you all, and I hope your holidays are amazing!”

When you can’t be together in person, a warm and heartfelt greeting can help bridge the distance.

“Even though we’re not together this Christmas, you’re always in my thoughts. Wishing you a holiday full of love, laughter, and all the little things that make the season special. Miss you tons!”

“The holidays don’t feel the same without you, but I’ll be enjoying all our favorite traditions and thinking of you. Sending hugs, love, and wishes for the best Christmas ever!”

If your relationship with certain family members is complicated, you can still send a message that’s warm but keeps things simple. And if you need help for managing the anxiety that comes with the holidays, here are 10 tips to cope.

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas and a New Year full of happiness. Hope the holidays bring plenty of reasons to smile!”

“Merry Christmas! I hope this season brings you joy, peace, and lots of great food.”

“Thinking of you this Christmas and wishing you all the best. I hope your holidays are full of love and laughter.”

💙 Get in the holiday spirit when you sit down to write by listening to the Holiday Family Reunion playlist.

Whether they’re the ones you’re catching up with over cocoa or the people you’re texting memes to at 2 am, friends add so much to life. Let them know just how much color and joy they bring you, and how much you appreciate them.

For the friends who are practically family, a heartfelt but casual message can show how much you value them.

“Merry Christmas! You’ve been the best part of this year. (Well, you and snacks.) Here’s to more laughs, fewer bad decisions (or maybe more!), and plenty of good times ahead.”

“Happy holidays to my ride-or-die. Thanks for always having my back and knowing exactly how to make me laugh. Hope your Christmas is as awesome as you are!”

“Merry Christmas to the friend who makes life way more fun. I couldn’t have survived this year without you — and I wouldn’t have wanted to, either!”

Even if you’re not super close, a thoughtful holiday message can let casual friends know you’re thinking of them.

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas and a New Year filled with great vibes, good people, and good times.”

Happy holidays! Hope your season is filled with just the right amount of chaos, laughs, and corny holiday sweaters.”

“Merry Christmas! Here’s hoping Santa brings you all the good stuff — and maybe a break from the holiday madness.”

The holidays are a great time to reach out to friends you don’t see as often but still care about. A message like this can help you reconnect.

“It’s been too long! I miss having your vibes in my life. Merry Christmas, and let’s make this the year we actually get to see each other.”

“Thinking of you this Christmas and all the great times we’ve shared. Hope your holidays are as fun and wonderful as you are. Let’s catch up soon!”

“Merry Christmas! Hope your holiday season is full of laughter and good memories. You’ll always hold a special place in my heart.”

“I always think of the most important people in my life at this time of year, and that includes you.  Sending you lots of love and hoping your Christmas is amazing. Let’s talk soon.”

When miles separate you, a thoughtful holiday message can remind your faraway friends that you’re still connected.

“Merry Christmas from across the miles! Missing you tons and raising a glass to all the good times we’ve shared. Can’t wait to catch up soon!”

“Happy holidays to the friend who makes the distance feel smaller. Hope your Christmas is as wonderful as you are, and here’s to making new memories in the new year (even if they’re mostly virtual!)”

“Even though we’re far apart, you’re one of the best gifts in my life. Sending you love, laughter, and this cheesy holiday card.”

If humor is your friendship language, keep your message lighthearted and fun.

“Happy holidays to the friend who always knows how to make me laugh — even when the eggnog is terrible and your Christmas sweater is even uglier than last year. Let’s make 2024 just as ridiculous!”

“Here’s to a Christmas that’s full of laughs and chaos — just like us! Hope your holidays are as fun as that time we [insert your funniest shared memory].”

For the coworkers who turned into your go-to people, a little festive cheer can go a long way.

“Merry Christmas to my favorite office buddy-turned-actual-friend. Thanks for making work (and life) way more fun. Hope your holidays are amazing!”

“Happy holidays! You’ve survived the year with me, so I’m pretty sure you can handle anything. Wishing you the best Christmas ever, [desk-buddy/work-spouse]!”

“Merry Christmas! I’m so glad work gave me at least one good thing this year — our friendship. Hope your holidays are full of laughter and relaxation. Here’s to more office antics in the new year!”

💙 This holiday season, learn to nurture happier and healthier relationships with Tamara Levitt’s Relationship with Others series.

Love has a way of making the holidays feel even more special. Whether you’re celebrating together, apart, or just starting to connect, the right words in a Christmas message can make your special someone feel important.

Your partner is likely at the center of your holiday celebrations, and Christmas is the perfect time to remind them how much you appreciate their love and support. Here are some ideas to inspire your message.

“Christmas wouldn’t be the same without you — and not just because you’re the one who always untangles the lights. Love you lots.”

“You’re still the best gift in my life. Thanks for keeping me sane, laughing at my terrible jokes, and being the amazing person you are. Merry Christmas!”

If your relationship is still in its early stages, a sweet and thoughtful message can show your excitement for the journey ahead without feeling too overwhelming.

“Merry Christmas! I’m so glad you’re part of my life — even if it means pretending I’m good at wrapping presents. Here’s to many more awkward holiday traditions together!”

“Happy holidays! This Christmas, I’m grateful for lots of things — good food, good times, and most importantly, you. Thanks for being amazing and sharing a little festive fun with me.”

“Dating you has been like finding a Christmas movie that's actually good: unexpected, occasionally ridiculous, but kinda magical. Hope your holidays are just as fun as you are.”

If you and your special someone are apart for the holidays, a loving Christmas message can help close the distance so you look forward to seeing each other again soon.

“Even though we’re apart, you’re still the person I think of when I hear corny Christmas songs. Missing you tons — but at least I don’t have to share my chocolate this year. Merry Christmas!”

“Wish you were here so we could argue about whether Die Hard is a Christmas movie again. I miss you, but I’ll settle for sending all my love and saving the debate for next year! (P.S. Die Hard is not a Christmas movie.)”

“Miles apart but always close in my heart (and on my phone screen). Can’t wait to see you IRL soon. Merry Christmas!”

If you’re engaged or recently married, this Christmas marks the start of a new chapter in your journey together. Celebrate it with a message full of love and excitement for the future.

“Our first [engaged/married] Christmas is here, and honestly, I think the biggest gift is that we survived putting up the tree together! Love you, even when we don’t agree on tinsel. Merry Christmas!”

“Merry Christmas to the person who agreed to marry me — proof that miracles really do happen. Let’s make a lifetime of festive memories together!”

“One tree + two Christmas stockings + three arguments about the best way to roast potatoes = our first married Christmas! Love you anyway. Here’s to forever, babe!”

If you’re expressing your feelings to someone you care about but aren’t in a relationship with yet, keep it light while showing your affection.

“Merry Christmas! You’re on my mind this season. I hope your holidays are as fun as you are — and maybe just a little less chaotic.”

“Sending you warm holiday wishes to someone who makes life a little brighter (even from a distance)!”

“Wishing you a Christmas full of good vibes and great food. You out-twinkle my tree lights.”

Coworkers are a big part of our daily lives, so spread a little holiday cheer around the office or your virtual workspace with a card or an email. Christmas greetings are a great way to show appreciation and sprinkle in a little warmth or humor into their day.

When you’re keeping it straightforward and professional, these messages are perfect for any coworker.

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas and a happy new year! Hope you have a relaxing holiday season — you’ve earned it.”

Thank you for all your hard work this year. Wishing you a wonderful holiday season filled with joy.”

“Happy holidays! It’s been great working with you this year. I hope your Christmas is merry and bright. Here's to even more success in the new year.”

For coworkers you know well and think of as friends, a personal touch can go a long way.

“Merry Christmas! Thanks for making work so much more fun. I’m looking forward to another year of laughs and great teamwork.”

“Happy holidays to my favorite teammate! Hope your Christmas is full of good food, great company, and plenty of well-deserved relaxation.”

“Wishing you a fantastic Christmas! Thanks for making the office a better place.”

If your workmates make you laugh, try a playful holiday message.

“Merry Christmas! May your holiday season be as stress-free as a Friday afternoon meeting cancellation.”

“Happy holidays! I hope Santa brings you everything you want this year — especially a new coffee machine for the break room.”

“Merry Christmas! Thanks for surviving another year of office shenanigans with me. Here’s to ignoring all emails over the holidays!”

If your team works across the world and connects virtually, a thoughtful holiday message can remind your coworkers you’re all still a team.

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas from afar! It’s been great working together, and I hope your holidays are full of joy and relaxation. It's time to close the laptop!”

“Happy holidays to one of the best remote teammates out there! Here’s to a new year filled with fewer Zoom glitches and more virtual coffee breaks.”

If you’re writing to your boss or manager, keep it warm, but professional.

“Wishing you a Merry Christmas and a wonderful holiday season! Thank you for your support and guidance this year — I’m looking forward to another exciting year ahead.”

“Happy holidays! I hope you have a relaxing and joyful Christmas. Here’s to a successful year ahead!

“Merry Christmas! Thank you for being such an inspiring boss. Wishing you and your family a season full of love, laughter, and happiness.”

If you want your Christmas greetings to feel more personal, think about what makes your connection with the person you're writing to feel unique.

Mention a shared memory from the year, like that hilarious inside joke from the office party, the big night out, or the epic road trip you took together.

Add a little humor or mention something that makes you both laugh, like their obsession with peppermint mochas or their questionable taste in holiday movies, to make your message stand out. Whether you’re sending a card or a text, writing something beyond “Merry Christmas!” can make it feel special.

If you’re feeling crafty, include a small photo, a doodle, or a festive sticker. These little touches can make your greeting feel more like you.

Writing a Christmas card for work doesn’t have to be stuffy and boring! Keep it polite and respectful, but friendly and positive too — and let your personality shine through. A safe approach is to express gratitude—like thanking your coworker for their teamwork, or your manager for their leadership—and add a kind wish for the holidays.

You could write: “Thank you for your support this year—it’s been a pleasure working together. Wishing you and your family a joyful and relaxing holiday season!”

If your workplace vibe is more relaxed, throw in a little humor: “Here’s to a holiday filled with good food, great company, and zero emails from me. Happy holidays!”

If your friend group loves a good laugh, let your holiday greetings reflect that. Here are some ideas to get you started. Personalize them by  thinking about what always makes your friends laugh, and tie it into the holiday spirit. If you share a favorite show, movie, or meme, reference it — it’ll make your greeting feel uniquely yours.

“Merry Christmas! May your holiday be as magical as finding the last parking spot at the mall on Christmas Eve.”

“Wishing you a Christmas that’s as great as your karaoke version of ‘Jingle Bells’ — so, basically unforgettable.”

The holidays are a time for inclusivity, so tailoring your message to fit the recipient’s traditions is always a thoughtful move.

If you know they celebrate Hanukkah, say “Wishing you a bright and joyous Hanukkah!”

For friends who observe Kwanzaa, “Hope your Kwanzaa is full of light, love, and celebration!” works beautifully.

And if someone isn’t religious, a kind and simple message like “Wishing you a peaceful and joyful holiday season” hits the right note.

If you’re unsure, go with something neutral like “Happy holidays” or “Season’s greetings.”

Digital greetings don’t have to feel impersonal. Start by using the recipient’s name (no “Dear Team” unless it’s unavoidable!) and add something that’s specific to your relationship. For example, mention a funny meme they sent, a virtual coffee chat you enjoyed, or a shared win from the past year.

If it fits your vibe, add a festive emoji, a fun GIF, or a quick voice message to liven it up. Video greetings are great, too — just record yourself wishing them a happy holiday with a little personalized touch. And if you’ve got a photo of a Christmassy experience you’ve enjoyed — like ice skating, mulled wine at a Christmas market, or volunteering at your local soup kitchen, attach it with a message.

Even if it’s short, a thoughtful line or two can go a long way. After all, the effort you put in makes digital greetings just as meaningful as a handwritten note.

The best salutation matches how well you know the person. Use their name when you can. It makes the card feel personal right away.

For family and close friends, try “Dear Mom and Dad,” “To our favorite neighbors,” or “Merry Christmas, Sarah and James.”

For casual notes, “Hi Aunt Lisa” or “Hey Ben, Merry Christmas!” fits well.

For work cards, “Dear Alex” or “Hi Maya and team” keeps the tone friendly and professional.

If you’re writing to a whole household, address everyone, like “To the Garcia family.”

End with a closing line that matches the warmth of your message, then add your name. A kind sign-off can make even a short card feel personal.

For family and close friends, “Love always,” “With love,” or “Big holiday hugs” feels natural.

For casual notes, “Sending love this Christmas” or “Merry Christmas” works.

For coworkers and professional contacts, “Warm wishes,” “Best holiday wishes,” or “With appreciation” keeps things kind without getting too personal.

Keep it warm for loved ones. Keep it friendly and brief for people you don’t know well.

#9511. The Creamy Sauce That Turns Your Turkey Sandwich Into A Louisville-Style Classic

America's home to a broad selection of iconic regional sandwiches, ranging from a Maine-style lobster roll to a Philly cheesesteak, with a signature sarnie in every state. In Louisville, Kentucky's noted induction is the hot brown, a broiled open-faced dish that originated during Prohibition. Creamy, decadent, and flavorful, this meal layers roast turkey atop crispy white bread, complemented with ingredients like lightly broiled tomatoes, bacon, as well as cheese. Especially essential is a smothering of creamy mornay sauce, which takes the dish from a turkey sandwich into definitively Kentucky hot brown territory.

This creamy liquid consists of flour, butter, and milk, meaning it's essentially a béchamel in its foundation. However, mornay sauce is further differentiated from béchamel by the addition of melted cheese, traditionally of a Swiss variety. Specific to a Kentucky hot brown, cooks often integrate the salty notes of Pecorino Romano cheese and occasionally a sharp white cheddar.

Whisked into the sauce after the creamy base has already formed, these bold-flavored cheeses serve as a crucial cornerstone flavor. The sauce is drizzled atop the other sandwich components, and the Kentucky hot brown is broiled to completion, finalizing the iconic rich and creamy dish.

Certainly, you can whip up mornay sauce to make a faithful Kentucky Hot Brown sandwich recipe, an application that won't disappoint. However, don't rule out using this flavorful thick sauce to enhance simpler sandwich builds, too. Roast turkey – the sandwich's star protein — goes terrifically with this dairy-based sauce, even without bacon, tomatoes, and other accouterments. So whether you're using up Thanksgiving leftovers or opting for store-bought roast turkey slices, toast some bread, throw on the bird, then round it out with the sauce on top. It's a pairing that makes for a satisfying meal.

A Kentucky hot brown is often enjoyed as a brunch dish, so even if you don't stick to the fully fleshed-out version, integrate ingredients often enjoyed during morning time. In addition to bacon, you could fry up an egg and trade the standard toast base for an English muffin. Or for a rendition a touch more inventive, wrap pieces of turkey into fresh crepes, then cover everything with mornay sauce. Stuffed with onions and mushrooms, such a dish lends the pairing a French touch, yet still showcases the beautiful combination of turkey and mornay sauce.

#9507. The Clothes That Make People Appear More Intelligent

How to use clothes to appear more competent.

How to use clothes to appear more competent.

Wearing more clothing makes you look more competent, a study finds.

Something as simple as taking off a sweater is enough to make you look less competent, the researchers found.

The finding applies to both men and women, said Dr Kurt Gray, the study’s first author:

“An important thing about our study is that, unlike much previous research, ours applies to both sexes.

It also calls into question the nature of objectification because people without clothes are not seen as mindless objects, but they are instead attributed a different kind of mind.”

The effect occurs because seeing more flesh encourages us to think about a person’s body, rather than their mind.

“We also show that this effect can happen even without the removal of clothes.

Simply focusing on someone’s attractiveness, in essence concentrating on their body rather than their mind, makes you see her or him as less of an agent [someone who acts and plans] more of an experiencer.”

Showing bare skin, though, does have some advantages, explained Dr Gray:

“A focus on the body, and the increased perception of sensitivity and emotion it elicits might be good for lovers in the bedroom.

Others appear to be less inclined to harm people with bare skin and more inclined to protect them.

In one experiment, for example, people viewing male subjects with their shirts off were less inclined to give those subjects uncomfortable electric shocks than when the men had their shirts on.”

“Even more than robbing someone of agency, the increased experience that may accompany body perceptions may lead those who are characterized in terms of their bodies to be seen as more reactive and emotional, traits that may also serve to work against career advancement.”

The study was published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (Gray et al., 2011).

#9505. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

#9503. 11 Chick-Fil-A Hacks That Make The Menu Even Better

Chick-fil-A doesn't have an official secret menu, like so many other fast food chains that boast must-try hidden items. But that doesn't mean you can hack the menu to come up with new and intriguing foods that arguably taste better than the items listed. In fact, despite its lack of hidden offerings, off-menu orders at Chick-fil-A are actually encouraged. It's a head-scratcher, but it's true. You can easily make substitutions and ingredient upgrades at Chick-fil-A, and in many cases, all you have to do is ask. The online ordering system will also facilitate some, so you don't even have to talk to anyone if you don't want to.

That said, the trickiest part of unlocking Chick-fil-A's off-menu items is figuring out the ones that are actually worth trying. That's okay, though, because we have you covered. After searching the company's website as well as troves of comments on social media and online forums, we managed to scrounge up a collection of Chick-fil-A hacks that will arguably make the menu even better. After all, more options are always a good thing.

Chick-fil-A is known for being one of a handful of fast food chains that serve the best mac and cheese. If you've ever tried it, you know why. It is cheesy, gooey, and the noodles are just right. Even so, that doesn't mean you can't customize it. You have a couple of options, too. The first ingredient addition the company's website recommends is Nuggets, either the classic or grilled ones. You could always just mix them right in as-is, but the pro move is to take them home and dice them up before stirring them into the mix.

In addition to enhancing the Mac & Cheese with chicken, you can also get a side of the Zesty Buffalo Sauce and Garden Herb Ranch Sauce and drizzle some of each over the top to make what is being referred to as Buffalo chicken mac and cheese. Heck, if you want to stay vegetarian, you can skip the chicken and turn up the flavors with just the sauces. Or, if you simply want some kick, go for the Buffalo, and you'll be all set. Either way, the Mac & Cheese is prime for ingredient additions. While not needed, they will absolutely add some spice to your life.

This next Chick-fil-A hidden menu item is perfect for picky kids or plant-based diets, but unfortunately, rumor has it that not all stores will accommodate the request. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, though, it's none other than a grilled cheese sandwich. It will have to be on a buttered, toasted bun, but in case you've never tried one that way, it is delightful — especially if the bun is flipped inside-out. Regardless, Chick-fil-A has both buns and cheese, so the ingredients are on hand.

Since creating a grilled cheese sandwich is a menu hack that requires quite a bit of accommodation from the kitchen, don't be surprised if some locations turn down the request. It never hurts to ask, though — unless, of course, the store is super busy. When the place is bustling and lines are building up, fast food secret menu etiquette says you should just stick to the regular menu so the staff can keep things moving.

The not-so-secret ice cream sandwich is a major creation that Chick-fil-A die-hards have been cashing in on for quite some time. Even if you are new to the hidden menu items, rest assured that this one is tried and true. Best of all, you don't have to ask an employee for any special favors — you can make this yourself, and because of that, it's possible at any location you visit.

While not on the official menu, another fun hack for the Icedream Cup involves adding fruit. Once again, you can pull this upgrade off yourself, and that's always a plus in our book. It's as simple as it sounds: All you have to do is order an Icedream Cup and a Fruit Cup, and combine the two. Mission accomplished.

The Fruit Cup comes with blueberries, strawberries, red and green apples, and Mandarin orange slices — all things that taste great paired with vanilla soft serve. Fruit cups come as they are, according to several employees online, but some places may be willing to withhold certain fruits from the cup if you ask. Either way, the combination of simple, sweet desserts is a winning one.

Chick-fil-A currently has three full-sized salads on the menu — a Cobb Salad, a Spicy Southwest Salad, and a Market Salad. The first features fried chicken nuggets, and the latter two are made with strips of grilled chicken — or at least that's how they are listed on the menu. As it turns out, you can easily customize the type of chicken on your salad depending on your mood and personal preferences. The online ordering system allows you to do so hassle-free.

When it comes to the chicken on your salad, you actually have quite a few options. For starters, you could always ask to leave the chicken off entirely, but something tells us the other variables will be most appealing for many people. Other than that, you have the option to choose between the classic Chick-fil-A Filet, a Spicy Filet, Chick-n-Strips, Nuggets, Grilled Nuggets, Grilled Filet (warm or cold), or a cold Grilled Spicy Filet. Whichever you are feeling, Chick-fil-A staff will be happy to make it happen. Or, as they say, it will be their pleasure, so feel free to customize the chicken on your salads to your heart's content.

Chick-fil-A features a whole lineup of tasty breakfast sandwiches, the most iconic of which is the Chicken Biscuit. However, it is admittedly a bit plain. Even if you order it with a spicy patty, it's still just chicken and a biscuit. You can easily fix that, though, and once again, you won't need to enlist an employee to help you. Simply order a side of hash browns to go with your breakfast sandwich (you were probably gonna do that anyway, let's be honest) and your favorite sauce. Then, dip a hash brown, or maybe two or three of them, into the sauce, open your sandwich, and add them as an extra layer. Not only will it streamline eating your meal, but it also adds tons of delectable texture and flavor. Sounds like a win-win to us.

You don't have to stick to the Chicken Biscuit for this menu hack, either. You can also apply it to the Chick-n-Minis, the Egg White Grill, the Bacon, Egg & Cheese Muffin, or any other breakfast sandwich that's calling your name. As for the sauces offered, Chick-fil-A has quite the collection. Anything from the Barbecue to the Garden Herb Ranch to the Creamy Salsa to the Avocado Lime Ranch and beyond has what it takes to improve your next breakfast sandwich.

The Frosted Lemonade at Chick-fil-A is what you order when you want a taste of soft serve, but still want bold, citrusy flavors to be the star of the show. It's pretty tasty on its own, but you can also take it a step further by asking to add strawberry syrup to the mix. We probably don't have to tell you, but lemon and strawberry are a match made in heaven, so combining the two flavors in Chick-fil-A's frozen drinkable treat is a no-brainer. We know it won't assuage any cravings for the discontinued fan favorite Frosted Key Lime Pie drink, but it might just help diminish the sting, even if only temporarily.

The online ordering system does not facilitate this upgrade, so the only caveat to this hack is that you will have to ask an employee. Fortunately, though, adding a swirl of strawberry syrup to the drink before they blend it up is simple enough that it shouldn't cause any issues. Well, aside from the fact that once you get a taste, you may never be able to drink one as-is again.

On Chick-fil-A's menu, you find a Berry Parfait, which features yogurt (duh) and a mix of fresh fruit. You can also order a Fruit Cup all by itself. But what if you only want yogurt? Well, the answer is simple — just order the Berry Parfait, hold the fruit. Or, better yet, ask for the fruit on the side. That way you can still enjoy it at a later time. Chick-fil-A isn't going to give you a discount because you order it without, so there's no need to sacrifice quantity.

Okay, we'll admit that this Chick-fil-A menu hack may seem a little obvious. After all, most places allow you to order menu items with ingredients removed. Still, sometimes a hack is so obvious that all you need is someone to point out that it's possible. Chick-fil-A-going yogurt lovers, rejoice!

Looking for a plant-based option? If so, the final Chick-fil-A menu hack that's worthy of your consideration is for you: Simply order a Cool Wrap without chicken. Typically, the wrap is made with grilled chicken, green leaf lettuce, and Monterey Jack and cheddar cheeses wrapped up in a flaxseed flour flat bread. Leaving the chicken off still leads to a yummy vegetarian-friendly meal (and if you add a side of Avocado Lime Ranch dressing or Jalapeño Salsa, even better). You can remove other veggies as well, but adding additional ones is likely a no-go — as usual it depends on location, but at worst, you can always ask.

In the morning, you can also order a Hash Brown Scramble Burrito sans meat to satisfy plant-based desires. Without the customary chicken, it features a blend of Monterey Jack and cheddar cheeses, scrambled eggs, and hash browns wrapped in a flour tortilla, so it's hearty enough to hit the spot.

#9500. McDonald's Workers Don't Scramble Freshly Cracked Eggs

The breakfast hours at a McDonald's restaurant tend to be quite busy, as commuters stop on their way to work for a specialty McCafé coffee or a McMuffin with its perfectly steamed (not fried) egg. And speaking of eggs, we know that McDonald's uses a freshly cracked egg in its McMuffins — but if employees aren't breaking open shells and dropping yolks for its scrambled eggs, what can they possibly be using instead for its Big Breakfasts? The answer is still eggs, but in another form.

For its breakfast platters, McDonald's employees use a liquid egg product from food supplier Cargill. That might sound kind of murky, but the only two ingredients in the liquid are actual eggs (from cage-free hens) and citric acid, the latter of which helps keep the color stable during cooking.

As for why McDonald's uses a liquid egg product for its scrambled eggs when there are actual fresh eggs right there, it could come down to volume, pace, and consistency. It does appear that there is more than one egg's worth in a portion of scrambled eggs, and it might just be quicker for employees to pour the liquid product onto the griddle. Using a liquid product also ensures the eggs look uniform after being cooked on the grill, which fresh eggs might not, as may have been the case with the folded eggs before they started arriving frozen.

If you were to step inside a busy McDonald's restaurant's kitchen at breakfast time, you would likely find a lot of organized chaos. Because while employees might be moving frantically to keep up with demand, many of the preparation and cooking processes tend to be automated and/or timed, like the gloriously greasy fries, making the work predictable, at least. And that is certainly the case with the scrambled eggs, which are made in a somewhat surprising fashion. Employees aren't actually scrambling the liquid egg product on an open flat-top using a turner; instead, the eggs are cooked in batches of up to four using a metal template called a scrambler.

The liquid egg gets poured into a ladle-like spoon that ensures equal amounts, and then those spoonfuls get deposited into the grid-like template, which is separated into four sections and sits on the grill. There is a plastic knob at the center, which the cook uses to manually agitate the template and create the scramble. And when the eggs are done cooking, the scrambler gets set aside, and the cook goes in with a spatula to remove the scrambled eggs and place them in a warming tray. All in all, the process takes an impressive 30 seconds or less.

#9499. A Nasty Sign Of Omega-3 Deficiency

A high omega-3 diet can lower the signs and symptoms of the disease by 50 per cent.

A high omega-3 diet can lower the signs and symptoms of the disease by 50 per cent.

Stiffness in the joints and swelling can be indirect signs of omega-3 deficiency, research suggests.

Waking up stiff in the morning, feeling pain in the joints, swelling, tenderness and loss of flexibility are all signs of arthritis.

Omega-3 deficiency could be contributing, as scientists believe there is a link between this leading cause of disability and a lack of omega-3 in the diet.

Researchers suggest that a diet rich in omega-3 could decrease the symptoms of osteoarthritis.

A study has found that adding fish oil to the diet — and to some degree flaxseed oil (alpha-linolenic acid has an anti-inflammatory effect) — can ease or even prevent osteoarthritis.

With population aging, osteoarthritis will be one of the leading causes of disability.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, by 2040 it is estimated that 26% of US adults aged 18 or older will be diagnosed by a doctor with arthritis.

While there are still no effective medications for treating this condition, omega-3 fish oil can be one of the best natural remedies in treating osteoarthritis.

Professor John Tarlton, the lead researcher of the study, explained the effect of omega-3 on osteoarthritis:

“Classic early signs of the condition, such as the degradation of collagen in cartilage and the loss of molecules that give it shock-absorbing properties, were both reduced with omega-3.

Furthermore, there was strong evidence that omega-3 influences the biochemistry of the disease, and therefore not only helps prevent disease, but also slows its progression, potentially controlling established osteoarthritis.”

Western diets contain high levels of omega-6 fatty acids, which can lead to inflammatory disorders such as colitis, heart disease, osteoporosis, cancer, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis.

Modern diets contain up to 30 times more omega-6 than omega-3, whereas our ancestor’s diets contained almost an equal level of these two omega fatty acids.

Therefore, supplementation with omega-3 can help to restore this imbalance in Western diets and improve conditions such as colitis and heart-related diseases.

Fish oil is much more effective than flax seed oil, but for vegetarians and vegans this supplement is an important option.

“Most diets in the developed world are lacking in omega-3, with modern diets having up to 30 times too much omega-6 and too little omega-3.

Taking omega-3 will help redress this imbalance and may positively contribute to a range of other health problems such as heart disease and colitis.”

The study was published in the journal of Osteoarthritis and Cartilage (Knott et al., 2011).

#9498. Dolly Parton's Comforting Classic Casserole Starts With Potatoes And A Layer Of Onions

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Dolly Parton was a true country icon whose positivity spread far beyond music with her vast humanitarian work and, of course, her love for Southern cooking. A true foodie, this Tennessee gal might have been one of the best-selling artists of all time, but she retained her relatability to the end, even having a favorite Taco Bell order. And most likely because she famously grew up in a single-room cabin without the modern conveniences of running water or electricity, some of the recipes she has left us to remember her by are the ultimate in both cozy and frugal. One such example is a classic casserole that features just five ingredients, starting with sliced potatoes and a layer of onions, and is as comforting as a warm hug.

The remaining components are just as budget-friendly: ground beef, which gets precooked, a can of diced tomatoes, and chopped green bell peppers. Because there are so few ingredients in this casserole, it's important that you season well between each layer. A basic sprinkle of salt and pepper is all that's necessary, but you could also add a specialty blend like Kinder's Caramelized Onion Butter, available on Amazon, or the Sweet & Smoky seasoning from Aldi house brand Stonemill.

Another essential consideration is to layer the ingredients in the proper order. The potatoes must go in first so that when the beef and vegetables cook down, their juices are released, flavoring the spuds as they soak them up.

One of the best things about a five-ingredient casserole like Dolly Parton's is that it's wide open to customizations that will add your type of flavor to the dish. In terms of shortcuts, not everyone keeps potatoes on hand (they have a tendency to sprout eyes and then go bad before most people can use up a whole bag), but sliced canned potatoes are a shelf-stable option that you can keep in your pantry for whenever you need them. Because they're already cooked, though, you'll want to reduce the overall bake time for the casserole by about half. Further, if you don't want to bother with dicing and chopping green peppers and onions, you can pick up pre-cut tubs in the produce section of most major grocery stores.

Now for customizations. Cheese makes everything better, so if you have a bag of shredded cheddar or even pepper jack for a little hit of spice, top the casserole with it before baking. Over on Reddit, some commenters had ideas for dressing this dish up thematically. "The nice thing is, it was meant to be adaptable," one user wrote; they suggested adding taco seasoning and sauce between the layers for a Mexican-themed "taco casserole," or tossing in a can of kidney beans and chili seasoning for a (you guessed it) chili version. If the dish is too simple for you as-is, you can treat it as a jumping-off point for your creativity in the kitchen.

#9497. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9494. Struggling with impulse control? Try these 7 tips

Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA

You send the text before you finish thinking it through. You put in an online order before asking yourself whether you really need it. You eat three bites of the snack before you realize you’re not even hungry.

Impulsive moments like these aren't signs of a character flaw. They reflect your brain's tendency to act before it fully evaluates the consequences. For some people, that tendency shows up during a stressful stretch and eases once life calms down. For others, especially those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), it's more of a constant struggle. Either way, impulse control is a skill you can improve.

So, what does this mean for you? Let’s break down what drives impulse control, and what you can do about it.

Impulse control is your ability to pause before you act on an urge, thought, or emotion — that split second where you decide whether to follow through.

Your prefrontal cortex, the part of your brain responsible for planning and thinking ahead, mostly handles this. When it's working well, it helps catch an impulse before that impulse becomes an action.

If your impulse control feels shaky at times, that’s not necessarily a willpower problem. It usually means your brain is under strain from stress, poor sleep, or emotional overload.

Most people who act impulsively on occasion don’t have a diagnosed disorder. For others, though, struggling to resist harmful urges is a persistent pattern. Impulse control disorder covers conditions like intermittent explosive disorder (sudden, disproportionate anger), kleptomania (compulsive stealing), pyromania (compulsive fire-setting), and compulsive gambling. These conditions may respond well to professional support, such as therapy or medication.

Your brain relies on two systems that don't always agree. The limbic system reacts fast, driven by emotion and instinct. The prefrontal cortex works slower, weighing your options before you act.

When you're calm and rested, the prefrontal cortex can keep impulsive urges in check. When your brain is pushed past its capacity, the limbic system takes over instead. Impulse control shifts throughout the day depending on how you're feeling, which is why the same urge can feel manageable to sit with one moment and impossible to resist the next.

A few factors can make impulse control harder:

sleep deprivation, which weakens your brain's ability to regulate behavior

chronic stress, which keeps your brain in a heightened, reactive state

strong emotions that feel too intense to ignore or resist

substance use, which affects your brain's decision-making centers

ADHD and other neurodevelopmental conditions, where pausing may be a challenge throughout daily life, not just under pressure

Like any skill, impulse control strengthens with practice. The tips below work at different layers: some help in the moment, while others ease the mental strain that makes urges harder to resist in the first place. Feel free to start with one or two that feel relevant to you.

Impulsive urges can feel pressing, but they don’t have to dictate what you do next. Often, just pausing for a moment is enough to break the pull.

Try: Counting to ten, taking a slow breath, or naming what you're feeling out loud. Some people find a go-to phrase useful, such as "not yet" or "wait and see" to delay their response. Over time, this habit starts to feel more natural.

💙 Learn how to Resist Emotional Urges with Dr. Julie Smith on Calm.

Most impulsive behavior follows a pattern. It tends to spike around conflict, boredom, overwhelm, hunger, or fatigue. Once you learn your triggers, you can work with them instead of reacting in the moment.

Try: Keeping a brief log for a week or two. Note when impulsivity shows up, what leads to it, and how you feel. Once you spot a pattern—say, you're most reactive before meals or after a difficult conversation—you can plan around it.

Eat before that difficult conversation. Save demanding tasks for your sharper hours. Take a breath before responding to messages that tend to trigger a reaction.

💙 Discover Dr. Judson Brewer’s Breaking Bad Habits masterclass on Calm.

Under pressure, your brain defaults to what's fast and familiar. If-then planning gives it a prepared response instead, so you're not improvising when emotions are running high.

Try: "If [situation], then I'll [response]." For example, "If I feel the urge to reply right away, then I'll wait 10 minutes first." Or "If I'm about to make an unplanned purchase, then I'll add it to a list and revisit it in 48 hours." The more specific the plan, the harder it is to talk yourself out of it later.

💙 Walk through this process with Calm’s If-Then session with Jay Shetty.

Impulse control runs on limited fuel: sleep, stress, and mental bandwidth all shape how much of it you have on a given day. That's why impulsive urges tend to show up most at the end of a long day or after a stretch of bad sleep.

You can't eliminate every source of strain, but you can cut down on low-stakes daily decisions. Try prepping meals or laying out clothes the night before — that way, you're not making choices when you're already running on empty.

It’s also worth protecting what restores you, including sleep, movement, time away from screens, and nourishing meals.

Struggling with too many decisions? Here are 8 tips for when your mental energy is low.

Regular mindfulness practice builds your ability to pause as an ongoing habit, not just in the moment an impulse hits. Start with a few minutes a day, and keep at it on a schedule that works for you.

Try: Focusing on your breathing during practice. When you notice an urge come up (to shift position, check your phone, stop early), gently return your attention to your breath instead of acting on it.

💙 Start with the Basics of Mindfulness from the 7 Days of Calm series.

New habits can be tempting to abandon in the moment. Outside structure, like asking someone to check in on you, gives you accountability beyond your own willpower.

Try: Telling someone about the pattern you're trying to change. Even saying it out loud can make it harder to slide back into old habits.

If you’d rather handle this on your own, here are 6 ways to hold yourself accountable.

If your impulsivity is a constant pattern that impacts your relationships, work, and daily life, self-directed strategies may not be enough.

A therapist trained in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) can help you identify what's driving your behavior and develop more effective responses. If ADHD is part of the picture, an assessment can open the door to options like medication.

If you're not sure where to start, your primary care provider is a good first stop.

Poor impulse control can look like interrupting people mid-conversation, buying things without thinking it through, snapping in anger, or acting on cravings without a second thought. It tends to show up most when you're under pressure, drained, or emotionally overwhelmed.

If you have ADHD, tools such as if-then planning give your brain a prepared response before the moment of temptation arrives. Consistent mindfulness practice can also help you build the capacity to pause in those moments.

If impulsivity is getting in the way of your work, relationships, or daily life, it's worth talking to your doctor or an ADHD specialist. For some people, medication can meaningfully help.

Impulse control disorder may involve anger that feels bigger than the situation calls for, compulsive stealing, or gambling that's negatively impacting your life. If resisting an urge feels out of your control, that's worth bringing to a doctor — this condition is treatable.

Stress puts your brain into threat-response mode, which interferes with the part of your brain that handles careful decisions. That heightened stress state is useful in an actual emergency, where speed is more important than reflection. But in everyday situations, it makes thoughtful decision-making harder.

Mindfulness trains the same skill impulse control relies on: noticing an urge without immediately acting on it. Regular practice improves attention and emotional regulation, which makes it easier to find that pause in tempting situations. This can be especially useful if you have ADHD or you’re working on substance-related impulsivity.

Check out how a regular mindfulness practice can support your overall mental well-being.

The amount of time it takes to improve impulse control depends on your situation and your approach. Tools such as if-then planning or pausing before big decisions can help within a few weeks, while mindfulness and therapy tend to take longer — often several months of consistent practice.

Self-control is broader than impulse control: it covers habits like managing emotions and staying on task. Impulse control is more specific: it's about what you do in the gap between having an urge and acting on it. You can have strong self-control overall and still struggle with impulses in the moment, or be quick to pause in the moment while your broader self-control could use work.

Mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

#9491. 5 Common Prescription Drugs Linked To Memory Loss

Prescription drugs taken by millions of people around the world can affect memory.

Prescription drugs taken by millions of people around the world can affect memory.

Memory loss is not always a result of ageing.

Here are five types of drugs that can affect memory.

The older type of antidepressants — known as tricyclics — have been linked to memory loss.

Around half of people taking them report problems concentrating and one-third say they have memory loss.

Benzodiazepines include drugs marketed under the names Valium, Ativan, Klonopin and Xanax.

These drugs are often prescribed for anxiety and other mental health issues such as OCD, insomnia and post-traumatic stress disorder.

Unfortunately they are also linked to memory loss and even Alzheimer’s.

Dr Helene Alphonso, a psychiatrist and Director of Osteopathic Medical Education at Texas University, said:

“Current research is extremely clear and physicians need to partner with their patients to move them into therapies, like [modern] anti-depressants, that are proven to be safer and more effective.”

Statins are prescribed to many people to keep their cholesterol in a safer range.

The Food and Drug Administration lists memory loss, forgetfulness and confusion as possible side-effects of the drug.

Some people do report memory problems when taking them, but the studies conducted so far are inconclusive.

Beta-blockers slow the heart rate and are used to lower blood pressure.

They are also prescribed to those with congestive heart problems.

Beta-blockers, though, may also cause the loss of emotional memories.

They have even been tested as a way of treating post-traumatic stress disorder because of their ability to block emotional memories.

Again, though, the studies are not conclusive.

People who cannot sleep are sometimes prescribed so-called ‘Z-drugs’.

The ‘Z-drugs’ have been linked to memory loss: especially losing the ability to make new memories.

They have also been reported to cause strange behaviours like driving or cooking with absolutely no memory of the event.

Where possible consider a psychological therapy or applicable alternative to using these drugs.

Naturally, you should always consult your physician before making changes to your medication.

Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean

#9489. Canned Clam Chowder Is 100x Richer When You Add This Creamy Ingredient

Clam chowder is one of those rich, indulgent soups that sticks to your ribs and leaves you feeling utterly satisfied by the time you've worked your way through a bowl. And while there is something intangibly special about a homemade chowder, many of us don't have the time or wherewithal to spend chopping and simmering, nor access to fresh clams, so more often than not, we're reaching for a canned version. And the store-bought stuff is definitely a serviceable substitute (it even makes a flavorful seafood pasta sauce), but if you want to make it 100 times richer and much closer to homemade, adding a pat or two (or five) of butter gives it an instant upgrade.

New England-style clam chowder is creamy by default, and while the canned version typically gets that right, the flavor can fall a little flat at times or have too much of the wrong things. Adding butter can actually help remedy a multitude of sins, like excessive saltiness, which is why you'll likely want to use unsalted butter, as canned soups tend to be fairly high in sodium already. Butter can further help mellow your soup's underlying sourness, bitterness, or too much acidity, in addition to creating a deeper, richer backdrop for the bits of potato and clam. It also facilitates a more velvety, silky texture that will make you want to lick the bowl clean.

Adding butter to clam chowder to improve the texture and the taste is pretty straight-forward, but there are a few things you'll want to keep in mind. First, to avoid the butter breaking and separating, you should add it at the end of the soup-heating, after the pot has been taken off the burner. Further, instead of aggressively stirring the butter in, you might instead let it melt slowly into the soup, holding the pot by the handle and tilting it around at different angles until the golden pat has disappeared, so that it has the opportunity to gently incorporate into the chowder.

If you go rummaging through your fridge looking for butter but come up empty, there are a few ingredients you might have on hand that can add their own brand of richness. Heavy cream is one option, which will create a spoon-coating thickness. You might also mix in a dollop of plain yogurt, which can give the chowder a pleasant tang. And a surprising addition is Cheez Whiz. One commenter on Reddit vouches for this ingredient, which they said not only makes the chowder creamier and richer, but also gives the soup a desirable bite with its sharp, cheesy flavor.

#9486. Not Plain Butter: The Flavorful Topping Bobby Flay Recommends For Ribeye Steak

While Bobby Flay never sleeps on technique, he's famous for pairing unorthodox, potent seasonings with classic recipes. His use of gochujang on ribeye is no different, and while he often reaches for it for a steak glaze, he also loves to incorporate it into a compound butter for an easier, just as flavorful recipe.

Gochujang combines fermented soybeans, salt, chiles, and a wee bit of sugar into an all-in-one seasoning. The remaining ingredients in the compound butter, a mix of savory, sweet, salty, and aromatic seasonings, all work together to create a comprehensive blend that goes far beyond a simple finishing pat of butter. While some ingredients shine through the marbling of a ribeye, others contribute to the decadent richness most folks love in the cut. All the elements work together to create a full range of flavors that are easy to apply, especially if you make it ahead of time.

Adding butter at the end of cooking is an ideal way to prepare most steaks because it wraps the whole thing up with a final layer of moisture and the subtle sweetness of dairy fat, contributing to a velvety mouthfeel. But since ribeye already has ample marbling, Flay's gochujang compound butter ensures there will be plenty of new flavors to level it up even further. The intensity of the paste goes a long way toward cutting through the beef fat, ensuring your meal doesn't taste too one-note.

Butter is a bit delicate with heat, and compound butter is even more so. Applying Bobby Flay's gochujang mixture properly and allowing it just enough time to reach the right temperature is key to getting the most out of it.

One of the biggest disadvantages of cooking steak on a grill is that you can't mix butter with dripped juices and crispy burnt bits and then baste your beef. Still, Flay doesn't let that get in the way and gives the tops of his ribeyes a final smear with the compound butter before letting them sit on the grill for another minute or two. This gives the topping just enough time to melt over the meat. You can even move your steak to a cooler part of the grill and put the lid back on. Using a two-zone grill setup is ideal to keep your steak from overcooking while rendering all those final flavors.

Depending on your rub, you may want to make small tweaks to Flay's compound butter. Incorporating galangal rather than ginger introduces some added sharpness to cut through the heaviness of even the most well-marbled steak. If you want to lean into the heat, a sprinkle of gochugaru, a spice similar to gochujang, adds a bit of capsaicin without changing the flavor too much. Don't be afraid to add a bit of fish sauce to the compound butter, too, to beautifully beef up the umami notes in your steak.

This tender pumpkin crumb cake is for people who double the chocolate chips in pumpkin bread and the streusel on coffee cake. Atop the thin layer of spiced pumpkin cake lays a heavy blanket of buttery crumbs with a bold chocolate flavor, thanks to Dutch-processed cocoa powder.

Get the recipe: Chocolate-Pumpkin Crumb Cake

These Pumpkin Cupcakes, with their piped swirl of cream cheese frosting, are the ideal way to celebrate fall birthdays. The cupcakes are super tender, thanks to the addition of cake flour and oil. Sour cream and brown sugar add tanginess and molasses-y sweetness while also preventing the cupcakes from being dry.

For more cupcake decorating ideas, see our YouTube video: Decorate Cupcakes Better Than Ever.

My husband’s favorite fall dessert is Pumpkin Whoopie Pies, hands down. He can’t resist these subtly sweet cakes sandwiching rich cream cheese filling. This recipe has a few extra bells and whistles to take it over the top: Bread and Cake Enhancer to keep the cakes extra soft and fresh, xanthan gum in the filling to give it a smooth mouthfeel, and diced crystallized ginger for a bit of extra zing in the filling.

Either way, it’s great for snacking all day long.

#9481. The Difference Between McDonald's Big Mac & Burger King's Whopper

McDonald's and Burger King need no introduction. Both sit comfortably at the top of the fast-food game, and they have their burgers to thank for their global icon status. Even if you've never set foot inside either chain, chances are you've heard of the Whopper and Big Mac before. They're very different sandwiches, but have spent decades going head to head. The, excuse the pun, beef between the two chains has long been fast food lore. So what better way to settle things than by taking a closer look at what actually sets these heavy hitters apart?

Some differences you'll spot just by looking at the burgers side by side, like the Big Mac's two patties to the Whopper's one, or the extra bun hanging out in the middle of the Big Mac. Others you'll taste. Burger King famously flame-grills its patties, which gives the Whopper a smoky char, while McDonald's cooks the Big Mac patties on a flat griddle for a different, more seared flavor. Then there are the differences that are less obvious, and they have as much to do with history and branding as with what's beneath the buns.

Start with age. McDonald's traces its origins to 1940, well before Burger King's founding in 1954, yet the Whopper is the older burger by a significant margin. Then there's how each chain treats its flagship. Burger King has used the slogan "Home of the Whopper" for decades, so there's no question which burger is its standout. At McDonald's, the answer is less clear. The Big Mac is, of course, nothing short of iconic, dare we say even more so than the Whopper. But that lineup also includes the Quarter Pounder and the cult-favorite Filet-O-Fish, so it has to share the spotlight.

The Big Mac is nearly a whole decade younger than the Whopper. Invented in 1967 by Jim Delligatti, a local franchisee in Uniontown, Pennsylvania, it was first launched nationwide in 1968. The burger was born out of a practical need, with its double patties designed to give steelworkers — frequent customers at Delligatti's restaurant — a more filling meal after completing their shifts.

When it comes to the build, few burgers do things quite like the Big Mac. There are several things that set it apart from the Whopper. It features two beef patties, signature Big Mac sauce (frequently compared to Thousand Island dressing), shredded lettuce, American cheese, pickles, and onions. Already, there are some pretty glaring differences between the two — namely, they share just four ingredients: beef patties, lettuce, pickles, and onions. The Whopper also adds ingredients like tomatoes, ketchup, and mayonnaise. And if we're getting really nitpicky, even the onions are different; the Whopper uses sliced onions while the Big Mac opts for diced.

Obviously, there are two major differences we can't ignore. Firstly, there's the number of patties in each burger. The other is the number of buns. While the Whopper sticks to the standard two-bun setup, with everything wedged in the middle, the Big Mac uses three. The extra piece of bread, known as the club slice, isn't just there for show. Delligatti introduced the middle bun to help give the burger more structure, separating the two beef patties and making the towering stack easier to hold together. It also helps keep the sauce and other toppings from making the bottom bun too soggy under the weight of the fillings, giving the Big Mac its distinctive three-tiered construction.

Arriving a decade earlier than the Big Mac in 1957, the Whopper was created by the chain's co-founder Jim McLamore. It has since become Burger King's signature burger, spawning several variations over the years. These include the veggie-friendly Impossible Whopper, the barbecue-flavored Texas Whopper, and double- and triple-patty versions for those with a bigger appetite. At McDonald's, the Big Mac is something of a Lone Ranger, with no permanent variations on the classic burger offered on the standard U.S. menu.

Beyond their ingredients, another major difference between the Whopper and Big Mac is how the beef patties are cooked. McDonald's cooks its patties on a clamshell griddle before holding them in heated cabinets. Burger King, meanwhile, is famous for its flame-broiling method. Its frozen beef patties travel along a metal conveyor belt through a broiler, where open flames cook the meat. Many have argued that this smoky edge is what puts the Whopper ahead of the Big Mac in terms of taste. Plus, the Whopper claims to contain a quarter pound of beef, which beats out the Big Mac.

Both burgers also have slightly different nutritional profiles. If protein is what you're after, the Whopper has the edge. Despite containing just one beef patty compared with the Big Mac's two, a standard U.S. Whopper contains more beef by weight. That difference is reflected in their respective nutritional figures: A Whopper contains around 34 grams of protein, compared with approximately 25 grams in a Big Mac. This number further pales in comparison to the Triple Whopper, which contains a staggering 78 grams of protein, putting it comfortably in the ranks of the fast food burgers with the most protein.
